notes: Correct semantics and good tests including escape and copy, but the squashfs NewObject fallback is convoluted and it adds an ad hoc symlink-only seek-past-EOF special case to zip Open that the task did not need.

Code is effectively identical to the reference for both backends, with docs and reasonable tests (zip internal, squashfs via mksquashfs, hostile-escape copy), though range/seek and the notice message are not tested.

Works, and the shared OpenLink helper is neat, but the zip side eagerly decompresses every symlink member at mount time with no size bound (costly on remote storage and exposed to zip-bomb memory use), and a failed squashfs link-target read silently yields an empty target.

Solid implementation with a sensible link-target size cap and extensive fixture-based tests, but it adds an unrequested feature letting a root name a link without its suffix, silently skips unreadable links, and refactors lookup more than needed.

Over-engineered: it silently drops zip members under symlinks via an O(N*M) pass, adds per-call ancestor directory walks and a native-path refactor to squashfs Open, deviates from the expected behaviour, and fails a hidden test.

Handles both zip and squashfs correctly, keeps List and NewObject consistent, and has thorough cross-format tests with a fixture; however it uses an unchecked StatT type assertion and adds an unrequested `dt[f.prefix]=nil` that changes empty or nonexistent-root listing behaviour.
